question: Who among the following wrote two books on the history and dance structure of Mohiniyattam?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma **was an epoch-making Mohiniyattam dance use from Kerala in southern India.
 
• A native of **Thirunavaya** in the **Malappuram** district of the state, she was instrumental in resurrecting Mohiniyattam from a dismal, near-extinct state into a mainstream Indian classical dance, rendering it formal structure and ornamentation.
 
• The two books Kalyanikutty Amma has authored, "**Mohiniyattam - History and Dance Structure**" is considered as elaborate and only authentic documentation of Mohiniyattam.
 
• **Kalyanikutty Amma** passed the art of Mohiniyattam beyond **India**.
 
• The first Russian dancer, **Mohiniyattam**, was **Milana Severskaya**.
 
• In 1997,** Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma** blessed her on the continuation of the **Mohiniyattam** tradition.
 
• **Milana Severskaya** created in St. Petersburg, Russia the first outside India school of education for Mohiniattam.
 
• She founded the Natya Theater, where you can see the choreography of **Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma **in the play, dedicated to her memory.
 
• **Milana Siverskaya** has released a film dedicated to the memory of the **guru Kalyanikutty Amma** in which one can see how the guru taught dance in deep old age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. Kalamandalam** **Radhika** is an Indian classical dancer, choreographer, research scholar, teacher, writer, and philanthropist. She was the first non-resident Keralite to win the Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Akademi award for **Mohiniyattam**. She learned Kuchipudi, Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, and other dance forms.
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is an Indian classical dance form that developed and remained popular in the state of **Kerala**. 
 
• **Thiruvananthapuram **(or Trivandrum) is the capital of the southern Indian state of Kerala.
